tom_tat: Professor Quan and his wife, both 55, have three strikingly beautiful daughters aged 25, 23 and 20 who are all mute from birth, leaving their learned parents heartbroken until a Dharma talk on cause and effect reveals the karmic debt behind it.

A noodle shop in northern Thailand grows rich on its addictively delicious broth, but when the secret leaks it proves to be frog soup, and the owner who personally slaughtered countless frogs ends up with a frog-like face, tormented by visions of frogs before dying in madness.

When the promising young doctor Truong Vi Luc takes his own life, investigators discover female hormones overwhelming his body after six years of eating hormone-laced chicken, compounded by his grandfather's lifelong trade of castrating pigs and chickens — a stark case of karmic retribution.

After Mr. Luong and his wife rescue a drowning dog, it brings them fortune and twice lays down its life to save their little son, so the grateful family holds a solemn seven-day funeral for the loyal animal — a living lesson in gratitude and good retribution.

tieu_de: Story 05: The Man Who Loved to Fish
tom_tat: An avid angler's fishing club falls apart after two chilling events: one member chokes to death on a fish hook hidden in a fish's innards, and its champion suffers a crash that leaves his mouth torn like a hooked fish's — until repentance before the Buddha heals him.

A farmer who invents a cruel dish of live baby fish stuffed into hollow vegetables loses all three children in a fire, the eldest hiding his siblings in water jars just as he once trapped fish — a devastating lesson in karmic retribution that drives him and his wife to monastic life.

tieu_de: Story 07: The Man with Elephant Legs
tom_tat: A merchant who for years roasted live geese on a red-hot iron table to make a tonic of their legs develops swollen, elephant-like legs racked with pain for six years, until sincere repentance toward Heaven and a vow of lifelong vegetarianism finally stills the suffering.

A produce dealer quits the lucrative skink trade after witnessing the To Vuong family's cruel mass slaughter of live skinks — and then their horrifying deaths in a mountain crash that mirrors exactly what they did to the animals, down to the staring eyes and the impaled body.

A young man dies when a live mountain-crucian lodges in his throat, and seven days later his father dies identically on cremation day; then a hospital director recounts Van Lai, who ate live turtles piece by piece and lost limbs to five amputations — proof that those who hook fish get hooked in turn.

A bride nicknamed "Miss Monkey" stuns guests with her beauty on her wedding day, but the white gloves hide a secret: a left hand with only stumps, retribution for her father severing a pleading monkey's fingers while her mother watched seven months pregnant.

tieu_de: Story 11: Cutting Corners and Skimping Materials
tom_tat: A corrupt official forces an honest builder's family into shoddy construction that collapses in a storm, destroying the family name; years later the official dies buried with his kin under his own birthday villa, built with the same stolen-material trick he taught his son.

A devoted wife sacrifices everything, even her health, to fund her husband's doctoral studies in Japan, only to be betrayed, framed, and driven with her little daughter to suicide in Yokohama — until Heaven's retribution strikes the ungrateful husband blind and senseless mid-lecture on marital happiness.

tieu_de: Story 13: The Strange Case of the Judge
tom_tat: A retired judge notorious for 28 years of bribery, lust, and wrongful verdicts is found disemboweled in a cave by three dogs while his deranged daughter plays beside the corpse — Heaven's execution where human law never reached him.

A village girl lured from the mainland by traffickers posing as bride-seekers is forced into prostitution and ruin in Taiwan, but her tormentors cannot escape: haunted nightly by their victims, one goes mad and the other two die of AIDS in America — evil profits ending in terror and pain.

The jolly owner of Taipei's famous "High-Class Delicacy" roast-duck empire suddenly collapses mid-service, quacking like a duck for three days and nights before dying with blood streaming from every orifice — and every branch of the shop closes with him.

An angler on the Liao River hooks not a big fish but a mother turtle clung to by her babies, whose bodyguard-like devotion reminds him of his own childhood love for his parents — so he frees them all, snaps his rod, and becomes a faithful Buddhist who urges others never to kill.

tieu_de: Story 17: The Tale at the Logging Camp
tom_tat: A logger with a cruel habit of flinging hooked fish skyward to smash on the ground dies exactly the same way, snagged by a crane, lifted high, and dropped to his death — a retribution so exact his fellow workers give up fishing.

tieu_de: Story 18: When the Slaughter Machine Was Done
tom_tat: An engineer who invents an automatic pig-slaughtering machine is snagged by his own invention at its first demonstration and processed into neat portions in minutes, recalling how the great hunter Hemingway died by his own beloved gun.

A virtuous Bodhisattva-precept vegetarian of 30 years is reborn as a piglet because her dying thoughts clung to killing a pig for her grandson's wedding feast, teaching that whatever thought grips the mind at death decides rebirth, outweighing a lifetime of merit.

A Shanghai gourmet who boils a live turtle and pours searing sauce down its throat dies in a house fire with his head wedged in iron window bars, gulping the firefighters' scalding spray — tasting exactly the torment he dealt the turtle, a vivid "retribution in this very life."

tieu_de: Story 21: The Love of the Golden-Haired Monkeys
tom_tat: A 65-year-old monk recalls his hunting youth, when a mother monkey begged with gestures to be shot in place of her baby, moving him to lay down his gun — while his sharpshooting friend who loved destroying nests died fallen in a ditch, his corpse picked apart by the very creatures he killed.

A merchant who murders his employer in a staged car crash to seize his fortune and wife ends up ruined by the very son born of that union, who squanders everything on drugs and cannot even afford his father's coffin — the family destroyed root and branch.

A devout Buddhist volunteer who for years tenderly washes and chants for the unclaimed dead in a Brazilian morgue later prospers into wealth through honest work, raising filial, accomplished children who carry on her charity — good causes reaping good rewards.

In Qing-dynasty Beijing, a fierce donkey that only its owners can ride is revealed in a dream to be repaying a past-life debt of 300 coins to a borrower, mile by mile — a classical tale of exact karmic bookkeeping.

A true Song-dynasty tale of Princess Thang Hoa, who murders her husband's first wife and silences the witnesses, and is reborn centuries later in Taiwan as My Le, where her victims' ghosts return to claim her life until repentance, the Emperor Liang Repentance, and Amitabha Buddha's deliverance set all free.
A brief introduction to the Chu Tu Hoa borrowed-body case, translated from Taiwan's "Today's Buddhism" magazine with plain-language narration by journalist Ly Ngoc.
noi_dung: {align:justify|(Translated from Taiwan's "Today's Buddhism" magazine. Plain-language narration: journalist Ly Ngoc)}

tom_tat: The author's afterword recounts the meticulously investigated true case of Chu Tu Hoa, an 18-year-old Kinmen girl who drowned at sea and borrowed the body of a Mai Lieu villager's wife to return to life, proving the six realms and karmic retribution with living witnesses.
